headline: Hong Kong private banks add staff far slower than assets grow
body: Assets at Hong Kong's private banks and family offices rose 24% last year to HK$12.9 trillion (about $1.65 trillion), while industry employment rose just 2%, with 10,140 staff in private banking and wealth management, according to Capco and the city's Securities and Futures Commission. Capco's Asia-Pacific insurance and wealth leader Simon Smallcombe attributed the gap to firms adopting technology, including AI, and said relationship manager numbers are not rising at the same rate.
note: An industry adding assets about 12 times faster than staff is a concrete read on what technology and AI productivity gains are worth to a bank's cost base. It also raises the bar for what one relationship manager is expected to cover.
correction: An earlier version said headcount grew 2.2%, from 9,920 to 10,140. The sources give 2% growth in industry employment and a headcount of 10,140; the 9,920 figure was not in them.
